title: Shared Treg dysregulation underlies psoriasis vulgaris and atopic dermatitis through the PHF19-PRC2 epigenetic axis.
authors: Lin, Yiting; Su, Xiaolei; Jin, Mingzhu; Wang, Yuqi; Li, Yaoyao; Zong, Bingquan; Song, Haoran; Lv, Yajie; Liu, Zhenhua; Wang, Gang; Wu, Shengxi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究银屑病与特应性皮炎共享的Treg失调及PHF19-PRC2表观遗传轴，聚焦免疫细胞亚群与药物靶点，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Psoriasis vulgaris (PV) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are chronic inflammatory skin diseases characterized by distinct dominant T cell subsets, yet emerging evidence suggests overlapping immune mechanisms. Whether a shared Treg abnormality underlies both diseases remains unclear. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing data from lesional T cells of 8 PV, 7 AD, and 7 healthy controls were analyzed. Treg subset identification, trajectory, communication, and enrichment analyses were conducted. Differentially expressed genes from both diseases were intersected and subjected to Mendelian randomization to screen for shared causal genes, followed by interaction mapping, drug prediction, and molecular docking. Findings were validated in Foxp3-tdTomato reporter mouse models of imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like and MC903-induced AD-like dermatitis by flow cytometry and quantitative PCR. RESULTS: A shared Treg triad remodeling pattern was identified: central memory Treg (cmTreg) was almost completely depleted, cycling Treg (Treg-c) expanded, and effector Treg (eTreg) accumulated in both diseases. Pseudotemporal analysis revealed a differentiation coordination defect, with upstream Treg-c shifting prematurely while effector Treg failed terminal maturation. Cell communication analysis identified enhanced MIF-(CD74+CXCR4/CD44) signaling as a shared intercellular remodeling axis, with the network shifting from a cmTreg-centric topology to one jointly centered on Treg-c and eTreg. Mendelian randomization identified seven shared causal genes (PDCD5, PHF19, GNAQ, LRR1, DHX36, TMEM107, FAM200B), with PHF19 serving as a core accessory subunit of PRC2. Molecular docking and in vivo experiments demonstrated that resveratrol binds PHF19, is predicted to activate the PHF19-PRC2-H3K27me3 axis, restores Treg subset homeostasis, and ameliorates skin lesions in both models. CONCLUSIONS: Treg subset remodeling is a shared pathogenic feature, nominating PHF19-targeted activation as a tolerance-restoring therapeutic strategy.
abstract_zh: 背景：寻常型银屑病（PV）和特应性皮炎（AD）是以不同主导T细胞亚群为特征的慢性炎症性皮肤病，但新出现的证据提示两者存在重叠的免疫机制。两者是否共享一种Treg异常尚不清楚。方法：分析了8例PV、7例AD和7例健康对照皮损T细胞的单细胞RNA测序数据。进行了Treg亚群鉴定、轨迹、通讯和富集分析。将两种疾病的差异表达基因取交集，并进行孟德尔随机化以筛选共享因果基因，随后进行相互作用图谱、药物预测和分子对接。在咪喹莫特诱导的银屑病样和MC903诱导的AD样皮炎Foxp3-tdTomato报告小鼠模型中，通过流式细胞术和定量PCR验证了发现。结果：鉴定出一种共享的Treg三联体重塑模式：在两种疾病中，中央记忆Treg（cmTreg）几乎完全耗竭，循环Treg（Treg-c）扩增，效应Treg（eTreg）积累。伪时间分析揭示分化协调缺陷，上游Treg-c过早转变，而效应Treg未能完成终末成熟。细胞通讯分析确定增强的MIF-(CD74+CXCR4/CD44)信号是共享的细胞间重塑轴，网络从以cmTreg为中心的结构转变为以Treg-c和eTreg共同为中心的结构。孟德尔随机化鉴定出七个共享因果基因（PDCD5、PHF19、GNAQ、LRR1、DHX36、TMEM107、FAM200B），其中PHF19作为PRC2的核心辅助亚基。分子对接和体内实验表明，白藜芦醇结合PHF19，预测可激活PHF19-PRC2-H3K27me3轴，恢复Treg亚群稳态，并改善两种模型中的皮肤病变。结论：Treg亚群重塑是共享的致病特征，提名PHF19靶向激活作为恢复耐受性的治疗策略。
